'''István T. Horváth''' (6 August 1953 – 7 March 2022)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cityu.edu.hk/chem/news/memory-prof-istvan-t-horvath-1953-2022 | title=In memory of Prof. István T. Horváth (1953-2022) &#124; Department of Chemistry }}</ref> was a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] American [[chemist]], working on greener and more [[green chemistry|sustainable chemistry]] since its inception.<ref name="green chemistry editorial">{{cite journal
 |doi= 10.1021/cr00033a600
 |author= Horváth, I. T.
 |year= 1995
 |journal= [[Chemical Reviews|Chem. Rev.]]
 |volume= 95
 |issue= 1
 |pages= 1
 |title= Introduction: Chemists Should Be Aware of the Environmental Implication of Their Chemistry}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal
| pmid = 22879509
| year = 2012
| last1 = Tuck
| first1 = C. O.
| title = Valorization of biomass: Deriving more value from waste
| journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]]
| location = New York
| volume = 337
| issue = 6095
| pages = 695–9
| last2 = Pérez
| first2 = E
| last3 = Horváth| first3 = I. T. | author-link3 = István T. Horváth
| last4 = Sheldon | first4 = R. A. | author-link4 = Roger A. Sheldon
| last5 = Poliakoff | first5 = M | author-link5 = Martyn Poliakoff
| doi = 10.1126/science.1218930
| bibcode = 2012Sci...337..695T
| s2cid = 715234
}}</ref> In particular, he focuses on [[homogeneous catalysis|homogeneous transition metal catalysis]] and in situ [[spectroscopy]]. He was highly involved and very influential in the now enormous field of fluorous solvents and technologies.<ref name="fluorous biphase catalysis">{{cite journal
 |doi= 10.1126/science.266.5182.72
 |author1=Horváth, I. T. |author2=Rábai, R. |year= 1994
 |journal= [[Science (journal)|Science]]
 |volume= 266
 |issue= 5182
 |pages= 72–75
 |title= Facile Catalyst Separation Without Water: Fluorous Biphase Hydroformylation of Olefins
 |pmid=17814001|bibcode=1994Sci...266...72H |s2cid=220107917 }}</ref><ref name="fluorous biphase review">{{cite journal
 |doi= 10.1021/ar970342i
 |author= Horváth, I. T.
 |year= 1998
 |journal= [[Accounts of Chemical Research|Acc. Chem. Res.]]

 |title= Fluorous Biphase Chemistry}}</ref><ref name=googlescholar>{{GoogleScholar|id=j2rKQ-MAAAAJ}}</ref>

==Education==
Horváth obtained his Diploma in [[Chemical Engineering]] (1977) and [[Ph.D.]] in Chemistry (1979) at [[University of Pannonia|Veszprem University]] in Hungary.

==Career==
Following his PhD, Horváth went on to spend time at [[Yale University]] as a [[Postdoctoral research]] associate (1982–1984), and as a Scientific Co-worker at [[ETH Zurich]] (1984–1987).  This was followed by a stint at [[ExxonMobil]] Corporate Research, Anandale, New Jersey (1987–1998).  He re-entered academia at the Institute of Chemistry in [[Eötvös Loránd University]], [[Budapest]] (1999–2009), and then became a Chair Professor of Chemistry and the Head of the Department of Biology and Chemistry at the [[City University of Hong Kong]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www6.cityu.edu.hk/bhdbapp/deptweb/profile/pith.html |title=Prof. István T. HORVÁTH |access-date=2010-08-06 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303213156/http://www6.cityu.edu.hk/bhdbapp/deptweb/profile/pith.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Research==
{{As of|2015}} his research lies in the conversion of biomass into platform chemicals, and the development of more sustainable fluorous solvent-based processes. He proposed that ''gamma''-Valerolactone (GVL) exhibits the most important characteristics of a sustainable liquid and it can be used for the production of both energy and carbon-based consumer products.<ref>{{cite journal | last1= Horváth | first1 = I. T. | last2 = Mehdi | first2 = H. | last3 = Fábos | first3 = V. | last4 = Boda | first4 = L. | last5 = Mika | first5 = L. T. | year = 2008 | title = γ-Valerolactone—a sustainable liquid for energy and carbon-based chemicals | journal = Green Chemistry | volume = 10 | issue = 2| pages = 238 | doi = 10.1039/b712863k }}</ref> It was confirmed by isotope labeling that fructose can be converted to [[hydroxymethylfurfural]] (HMF) then to [[levulinic acid]] (LA) and [[formic acid]] (FA) and finally to GVL in GVL as the solvent.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Qi | first1 = L. | last2= Horváth | first2 = I. T. | year = 2012 | title = Catalytic Conversion of Fructose to γ-Valerolactone in γ-Valerolactone | journal = ACS Catalysis | volume = 2 | issue = 11| pages = 2247–2249 | doi = 10.1021/cs300428f }}</ref> He is also the editor of numerous books and other peer-reviewed publications in the fields of catalysis,<ref>I. T. Horváth (Ed.) "Encyclopedia of Catalysis", Wiley–VCH, Weinheim, 2002.  {{ISBN|978-0-471-24183-6}}.</ref><ref>B. Cornils, W. A. Herrmann, I. T. Horváth, W. Leitner, S. Mecking, H. [[Hélène Olivier-Bourbigou|Olivier-Bourbigou]], D. Vogt (Eds.) "Multiphase Homogeneous Catalysis", Wiley–VCH, Weinheim, 2005.  {{ISBN|978-3-527-30721-0}}.</ref> green chemistry, and fluorous technologies.<ref>J. A. Gladysz, D. P. Curran, I. T. Horváth (Eds.) "Handbook of Fluorous Chemistry", Wiley–VCH, Weinheim, 2004.  {{ISBN|978-3-527-30617-6}}.</ref><ref>I. T. Horváth (Eds.) "Fluorous Chemistry", Springer, Berlin Heidelberg, 2012.  {{ISBN|978-3-642-25233-4}}.</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Horváth was made an Honorary Member of the Accademia Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti Modena in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.accademiasla-mo.it/soci-storici.php |title=Accademia Nazionale di Scienze, Lettere e Arti Modena |access-date=2016-03-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707181313/http://accademiasla-mo.it/soci-storici.php |archive-date=2017-07-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was elected Fellow of the American Chemical Society in 2014.<ref>[http://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2014-acs-fellows.html#P260_18987 American Chemical Society list of fellows]</ref>
